decisions.reason: The checks apply to different senders and authentication roles: a client's requested CertificateVerify versus a server's CertificateVerify.
The same alert outcome is triggered by different version violations: changing the HelloRetryRequest selection versus selecting a pre-TLS-1.3 version.
The enum mappings are for different ExtensionType fields and values: server_name=0 versus key_share=51.
The enum mappings are for different HandshakeType messages and values: client_hello=1 versus certificate_verify=15.
One forbids any client Certificate without CertificateRequest; the other requires an empty Certificate after a request when no suitable certificate exists.
The mappings constrain different AlertDescription fields and values: certificate_expired=45 versus certificate_unknown=46.
The same alert outcome is triggered by different version violations: changing the HelloRetryRequest selection versus selecting a version the client did not offer.
The transitions have different source states and inputs: WAIT_EE on EncryptedExtensions with PSK versus WAIT_CV on CertificateVerify.
The state transitions differ: WAIT_EE to WAIT_CERT_CR after EncryptedExtensions versus WAIT_CERT_CR to WAIT_CV after Certificate.
The first checks cookie-extension presence, while the second additionally requires exact preservation of the received cookie contents.
The mappings constrain different AlertDescription fields and values: bad_certificate=42 versus unsupported_certificate=43.
The client forms obfuscated_ticket_age by addition, while the server recovers ticket age by subtraction; these are opposite implementation operations.
The shared condition imposes two separate required mechanisms: (EC)DHE key establishment and certificate-based authentication.
The enum mappings are for different ExtensionType fields and values: padding=21 versus pre_shared_key=41.
The SignatureScheme mappings differ: ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256=0x0403 versus ecdsa_sha1=0x0203.
One excludes the RC4 cipher-suite family; the other excludes every cipher below 112-bit strength, a different prohibition.
Using supported_groups for group negotiation and using key_share for key agreement are separate extension-processing checks.
The SignatureScheme mappings differ: rsa_pss_rsae_sha384=0x0805 versus rsa_pss_pss_sha512=0x080b.
One requires the hash corresponding to the selected scheme; the other restricts where RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 scheme values may be used.
The sequencing checks concern different messages and flows: client Finished after server Finished versus EndOfEarlyData before client Finished.
The SignatureScheme mappings differ: rsa_pss_rsae_sha512=0x0806 versus rsa_pss_pss_sha384=0x080a.
The CertificateType mappings differ: OpenPGP_RESERVED=1 versus RawPublicKey=2.
The HandshakeType mappings differ: hello_request_RESERVED=0 versus server_hello=2.
The transitions have different source states, inputs, and destinations: Certificate drives WAIT_CERT_CR to WAIT_CV, while CertificateVerify drives WAIT_CV to WAIT_FINISHED.
The recording-window condition is a specific freshness mechanism, while failure of the general 0-RTT freshness determination is broader.
After ServerHello, changing the sending key to the handshake key and sending EncryptedExtensions next are separate state-machine actions.
A client Certificate response must echo the request context, whereas a server-authentication Certificate must carry a zero-length context.
One omits the server Certificate when certificate authentication is absent; the other requires CertificateVerify when certificate authentication is used.
Both impose the same 2 through 2^16-2 encoded-octet bounds on ClientHello.cipher_suites; the canonical evidence is the direct primary-body field definition.
The ExtensionType mappings differ: status_request=5 versus supported_versions=43.
The AlertDescription mappings differ: certificate_revoked=44 versus certificate_expired=45.
The placement rules constrain different extensions and message sets: max_fragment_length in CH/EE versus signature_algorithms_cert in CH/CR.
Although the bounds match, they apply to different fields: DistinguishedName versus NewSessionTicket.ticket.
One forbids interleaving other record types between fragments; the other forbids a key change within a fragmented handshake message.
The vector constraints apply to different messages and bounds: EncryptedExtensions.extensions at 0..2^16-1 versus ServerHello.extensions at 6..2^16-1.
Sending supported_versions in ClientHello and using supported_versions while processing ServerHello are different direction and behavior checks.
The HandshakeType mappings differ: encrypted_extensions=8 versus certificate=11.
Using supported_versions when processing ServerHello and sending that extension in ServerHello are receiver-side use and sender-side presence checks.
The SignatureScheme mappings differ: ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256=0x0403 versus ecdsa_secp384r1_sha384=0x0503.
The mandatory supported_versions presence checks apply to different messages: ClientHello versus ServerHello.
The AlertDescription mappings differ: certificate_revoked=44 versus certificate_unknown=46.
The CipherSuite mappings differ: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384={0x13,0x02} versus TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256={0x13,0x03}.
The ExtensionType mappings differ: server_name=0 versus cookie=44.
Both impose the same 1 through 255 encoded-octet bounds on PskKeyExchangeModes.ke_modes; the canonical evidence is the direct primary-body structure.
The same sentence imposes separate middlebox roles: verify the original server as a TLS client versus act as a compliant TLS server toward the original client.
The placement rules constrain different extensions and message sets: signature_algorithms in CH/CR versus ALPN in CH/EE.
Using supported_versions while processing ClientHello and sending supported_versions in ClientHello are different direction and behavior checks.
One forbids zero-length Handshake content; the other defines content length in terms of TLSPlaintext.length without imposing that nonzero constraint.
The ContentType mappings differ: invalid=0 versus change_cipher_spec=20.
The ContentType mappings differ: invalid=0 versus heartbeat=24.
The placement rules constrain different extensions and allowed messages: ALPN in CH/EE versus post_handshake_auth only in CH.
Selecting one of two exporter secrets for TLS-Exporter and deriving those secrets independently from traffic keys are separate checks.
The SignatureScheme mappings differ: ed25519=0x0807 versus ed448=0x0808.
One constrains the server's cipher-suite selection; the other requires the client to abort with illegal_parameter after receiving an unoffered suite.
The vector limits apply to different fields and bounds: certificate_request_context at 0..255 versus CertificateVerify.signature at 0..65535.
The record-boundary rule is instantiated for different handshake messages: ServerHello versus ClientHello.
The SignatureScheme mappings differ: ecdsa_secp384r1_sha384=0x0503 versus ecdsa_sha1=0x0203.
The SignatureScheme mappings differ: ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256=0x0403 versus ecdsa_secp521r1_sha512=0x0603.
The SignatureScheme mappings differ: rsa_pkcs1_sha512=0x0601 versus rsa_pss_rsae_sha512=0x0806.
Both require supported_versions in a TLS 1.3 ServerHello; the canonical evidence is the direct primary-body MUST statement.
The SignatureScheme mappings differ: ecdsa_secp521r1_sha512=0x0603 versus ecdsa_sha1=0x0203.
The ExtensionType mappings differ: server_name=0 versus signature_algorithms=13.
One controls whether the server sends CertificateRequest; the other controls whether the client sends Certificate after no request.
Although the encoded bounds match, they constrain different vectors: NamedGroupList.named_group_list versus CertificateRequest.extensions.
The NamedGroup mappings differ: secp521r1=0x0019 versus secp256r1=0x0017.
